features.name: Device enumeration page renders
features.description: Scenario 1 shows the MIDI title, description, an AUTO-DETECT INPUT toggle (default Off), a 'List all input devices' button, an input-device list, an 'OUTPUT' section with a 'List all output devices' button, an output-device list, and a status area.
expected_behaviour: AUTO-DETECT INPUT toggle is present and defaults to Off
'List all input devices' and 'List all output devices' buttons are present
Input list shows 'No MIDI input devices found!' when no external MIDI device is attached
Status region shows the red 'Please connect at least one external MIDI device...' banner

features.name: List all input devices button
features.description: Clicking 'List all input devices' enumerates MIDI input ports and populates the input list (or shows 'No MIDI input devices found!').
expected_behaviour: Clicking the button produces a visible change in the input list / status text

features.name: List all output devices button
features.description: Clicking 'List all output devices' enumerates MIDI output ports; the built-in 'Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth' appears in the output list.
expected_behaviour: Clicking the button lists at least 'Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth' in the output list

features.name: Auto-detect input toggle
features.description: The AUTO-DETECT INPUT ToggleSwitch enables/disables the device watcher. With no MIDI hardware attached, toggling produces no new visible text (no-op) — same in UWP and WinUI.
expected_behaviour: Toggle is interactive; state changes visually
With no hardware present, no new device text appears (parity no-op)

features.name: Receive messages page renders
features.description: Scenario 2 shows the description, an 'INPUT DEVICES' list ('No MIDI ports found' with no hardware), and a 'RECEIVED MESSAGES' list that displays incoming MIDI messages from the selected input device.
expected_behaviour: INPUT DEVICES section present and shows 'No MIDI ports found' with no hardware

features.name: Send messages page renders
features.description: Scenario 3 shows the description, an 'OUTPUT DEVICES' list (containing 'Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth'), a 'SEND MESSAGE' header, a Message Type combo (disabled until an output device is selected), and Reset/Send buttons (disabled until a valid message is composed).
expected_behaviour: OUTPUT DEVICES list shows 'Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth'
SEND MESSAGE header and Message Type combo present
Reset and Send buttons present but disabled until an output device + message type are chosen

features.name: Message parameter controls (dynamic)
features.description: Parameter 1/2/3 combos and the SysEx TextBox are Visibility=Collapsed by default and only appear after a message type is selected (which requires a selected output device / MIDI hardware). Identical XAML in UWP source and migrated app.
expected_behaviour: parameter1/parameter2/parameter3 and sysExMessageContent exist in XAML, collapsed by default
They reveal only after a message type is chosen (hardware-gated; not observable without a MIDI device)

features.name: Send / Reset buttons
features.description: Send and Reset actuate MIDI message sending. They are disabled (dead) until an output device and message type are selected; with no MIDI hardware they are non-responsive in the UWP golden as well.
expected_behaviour: Non-responsive when no output device/message type selected (parity with UWP golden; hardware-gated)
